question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: Five keyless GETs, 12:21:56.974Z to 12:21:58.108Z, labelled (B1) to (B5) here and named in the artifact, in that order, 'protected-resource doc, RFC 9728 path-inserted', 'protected-resource doc, well-known root', 'CONTROL: invented path under that prefix', 'authorization-server doc' and 'openid-configuration': the document at the RFC 9728 path-insertion URL, the same at the well-known root, an INVENTED path under the prefix as the control, the authorization-server metadata on the resource host, and openid-configuration there. No credential, no cookie, nothing registered.

decoded.two-documents: (B1) the path-inserted URL: 200, 124 bytes, sha256 73a8d0039805a0e70e2a06cd0c9a757e41058d9a016bc84e990b3c6594c736e7, declaring resource https://mcp.wix.com/mcp . (B2) the well-known root: 200, 120 bytes, sha256 2e4258184d5c7827d0087e30a01758127e4c2de8db94874e6c6ad7017e968751, declaring resource https://mcp.wix.com , the bare origin. Both name the single authorization server https://mcp.wix.com and the single scope offline_access. Two documents, two resource identities, one hostname.
decoded.the-control: (B3) an invented path under the same prefix, /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/9d4f1c20 (the token the re-run program fixes in its source; the withdrawn pass used de679bc6-not-a-resource and got the same 13 bytes): 404, 13 bytes of text/plain reading "404 Not Found", sha256 7d04f743..., which is also what openid-configuration answers on this host (B5). So on mcp.wix.com a 200 from this prefix IS evidence that the requested path is a declared resource. On mcp.figma.com the same control returns the host's one protected-resource document with a 200 (p-20261021-figma-prm-served-for-any-path-under-its-prefix); on mcp.asana.com it 404s with 9 bytes. Three hosts, two behaviours, and only the control distinguishes them.
decoded.the-authorization-server: (B4) https://mcp.wix.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server: 200, 519 bytes, sha256 9911ddca1205d5131feb7c8e1247e066dc69c933fc054bbec17d44116ccef0d4. Ten keys: issuer https://mcp.wix.com , authorize, token and register endpoints on the same host, response_types [code], response_modes [query], grant_types [authorization_code, refresh_token], token_endpoint_auth_methods [client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, none], revocation_endpoint equal to the token endpoint, code_challenge_methods [plain, S256]. A registration_endpoint is advertised and there is no client_id_metadata_document_supported key, which places this host in the dynamic-registration-only class of the census in issue #280, and the resource host is its own issuer.
decoded.what-a-client-would-send: A client that follows the challenge reaches (B1) and would send resource=https://mcp.wix.com/mcp . A client that guesses the well-known root instead reaches (B2) and would send resource=https://mcp.wix.com . Whether the token endpoint accepts either string is NOT measured: that needs a registered client and a token request, which is a credential and a write. The registry's surfaces.mcp value for this entry matches the document the challenge points at.
decoded.not-measured: Nothing behind the authorize, token, register or revocation endpoints. No client was registered even though registration is open.
decoded.artifact-withdrawn-and-re-measured: The transcript this record first cited, keyless-0604Z.txt, no longer exists and the URL answers 404: it was published by a container whose state commit was then lost, and the next publish from a restored container replaced the host's tree with one that did not contain it. Nobody outside that container ever read it, so it is withdrawn rather than relied on. Every figure in this record was re-measured keyless on 2026-10-22 between 12:21:55Z and 12:22:00Z by a published program, wix-keyless.py (sha256 a7e84359fef1cbb487d5fd1f66f292a6be553346dab96990ea3859b496fae70d), whose transcript is the artifactsUrl above; every status, byte count and SHA-256 of the owner-facing server, both metadata documents, the invented-path control, the authorization-server document, the site server's initialize and ten-tool list, the site GET and the vendor's example site reproduced exactly, the one exception being the HTML refusal page whose byte count is not reproducible by construction (see the controls above).

finding: mcp.wix.com serves TWO different protected-resource documents, and a control proves the difference is real rather than a catch-all: the RFC 9728 path-insertion URL returns 124 bytes declaring resource https://mcp.wix.com/mcp, the well-known root returns 120 bytes declaring the bare origin https://mcp.wix.com, and an invented path under the same prefix returns 404 with 13 bytes ("404 Not Found"), the same body openid-configuration returns. So a 200 from this prefix is evidence that the requested path is a declared resource -- the opposite of mcp.figma.com, which serves its one document for ANY path including an invented one (p-20261021-figma-prm-served-for-any-path-under-its-prefix), and in line with mcp.asana.com. The host is its own authorization server: 519 bytes of metadata, issuer https://mcp.wix.com, a registration_endpoint, token auth methods including none, PKCE plain and S256, and no client-ID-metadata key. Measured keyless 2026-10-22T12:21:56.974Z to 12:21:58.108Z; nothing was registered and no token was sought.
